tagline: From Stone City to the Mississippi, through Grant Wood country.
intro: From Stone City on the Wapsipinicon the byway runs about 80 miles east through Anamosa, Wyoming and Maquoketa to Bellevue on the Mississippi. The country is a patchwork of farmland and limestone bluffs strung between three rivers, the Wapsipinicon, the Maquoketa and the Mississippi, and the road passes through the painter's hometown and the settings that inspired him.

Stone City began as a quarry company town and built itself of stone, down to the station and the schoolhouse. Portland cement came along in 1905 and the quarries shut one by one. In 1938 the stone opera house was torn down for its stone.

moments.title: Stone City
moments.text: In 1932 Grant Wood and two friends started an art colony here on little more than $100, putting students up in a quarry owner's mansion while one founder lived in the water tower.

moments.title: Anamosa State Penitentiary
moments.text: Prisoners brought from Fort Madison began building it in 1873, with crenelated towers that give it the look of a medieval fortress, and it still holds inmates.

moments.title: Bellevue
moments.text: The town sits in a valley between North Bluff and South Bluff, with the Mississippi for its eastern edge and Lock and Dam No. 12 at hand.
